KIDS GAMES LESSON · KIDS GAMES · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Hot Potato — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches hot potato — the passing game played at comedy speed, where the loser&rsquo;s punishment is three frog hops.

What is this?

Hot potato is a circle passing game: pass the potato hand to hand while the music plays — and whoever holds it when the music stops does one funny task.

What does it mean?

Fast, gentle passing is a real skill — the handover — practiced here at a speed that makes everyone laugh when it goes wrong.

What does the child need to know?

You need a soft potato-substitute (a ball, a beanbag, an actual potato) and music you can stop mid-song. Three or more players in a circle.

Why this matters

The music makes the passing hurry, and the hurry makes the game — but the losing is so gentle (three hops!) that nobody dreads the stop.

What it teaches

Quick handovers, left-to-right passing order, watching the object move around the ring, and losing with a laugh.

Words to learn

potatohotpassquickcirclestophop

Say this to your child

“"Pass it quick, pass it quick — the potato is hot! Do not hold it, do not drop it — pass, pass, pass! Music stopped... WHO has the potato? Hop like a frog!"”

Step by step

  1. Sit in a circle, knees almost touching.
  2. Start the music and pass the potato one way — say which way first: "pass it left!"
  3. Pass it quick — the potato is HOT, do not hold it!
  4. The DJ stops the music at a surprise moment.
  5. Whoever holds it does the funny task — hop three times, or quack like a duck — then the music starts again and the potato flies.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, many hands surround the potato from every direction — the hands reach in fast because the passing never stops while the music plays.

Ask your child

"Which way are we passing?" "What do we do if the music stops on us?" (the funny task — and we laugh) "Can we pass faster?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might hold the potato with two careful hands like it genuinely burns, speed-pass so hard the potato flies across the circle, or beg for the hop task on purpose.

Out in the real world

Any circle of kids with any ball can start this game in one chant — "hot potato!" — and now your child knows both the passing and the kind-losing script.

Try it together

Two-potato round: two potatoes start at opposite sides of the circle and cross in the middle. Reverse round: the DJ shouts "change direction!" mid-song and the passing flips.

Understanding check

Ask: "What do we do while the music plays?" (pass it quick) "What happens to the holder when it stops?" (one funny task, then we play again)

This lesson pairs with the Hot Potato flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Kids Games.
